outcome: access to preferred postnatal contraception methods
cohort: The study population consisted of women who had completed a pregnancy in the previous 3 years.
finding: The uptake of postnatal contraception was low (38.7% for any method, 15.5% for LARC) with a fifth of women unable to access their preferred method, though younger age, lower household income, higher multiparity, operative delivery, unplanned pregnancy, and not breastfeeding were predictors of higher PNC uptake.
mod_finding: Operative delivery was a significant predictor of higher postnatal contraception uptake.
cross-section timing: Data was collected from women who had completed a pregnancy within the previous 3 years prior to the survey.
